scope: Surviving pre-1921 container identifiers and content-control leaves embedded in modern MSS EUR HODGSON volumes, linked where possible to RAS list states and modern shelfmarks.
central_claim: The 1921 dimension-based rebinding dispersed older shipment/container families, but original box/sack/bundle identifiers survived on paper surfaces and can be used to reconstruct historical relations across modern volumes.

control_surface.catalogue_description: Content of manuscripts from sack No. 8 of the original shipment; list of manuscripts relating to customs and manners of different ethnic communities.

surviving_member.title: Limbu text on traditional beliefs, rituals and prayers related to agricultural cultivation, harvesting and marriage
surviving_member.support: hand-made Nepali paper with a small mixed acidic section
surviving_member.catalogue_identifier_evidence: original sack number (8) is mentioned in Nepali on the title description

direct_edges.relation_strength: very high: same explicit historical sack number survives on control leaf and member object
direct_edges.historical_implication: A manuscript historically controlled under sack 8 is now bound in vol.85, whereas the sack 8 contents leaf is in vol.58. The historical container relation therefore crosses modern shelfmarks.
direct_edges.source_control: Do not infer that every ethnographic manuscript in vol.56-60 or vol.83-85 belonged to sack 8 without explicit surviving number or a legible sack-8 contents list.

Details of Contents of Bastas or Bundles in Trunk No.1 Cathmandu; includes Buddhism, Vaisavalis, Jatmalas, Army details, Catalogues & Sastras; later note says repacked in 1844 and put aboard the Hardwicke.

List of pictorial illustration of Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism on cloth and paper, with further list of papers in Trunk No.2, prepared at Darjeeling.
early_inventory_comparators.relation_to_crosswalk: late private-store trunk state before 1858 store list

early_inventory_comparators.description: Store list compiled in 1858 that became the list of MSS presented to the India Office in 1864; survives with copy of donation letter to Sir Charles Wood.
early_inventory_comparators.relation_to_crosswalk: closest handwritten precursor to 1864 institutional transfer manifest

early_inventory_comparators.description: Printed List of MSS Presented by Mr Hodgson to the India Office Library, with annotations.

source_control_rules: A repeated number across different inventory dates is not presumed identical until content is compared.
Modern adjacency is not evidence of historical co-custody after 1921 rebinding.
Historical co-custody does not prove direct textual descent.
Catalogue descriptions establish existence of old labels; exact wording and numbers should be checked on the physical/image object before diplomatic transcription.
Treat surviving cover/content leaves as archival artefacts in their own right, not merely catalogue aids.
next_actions: Inspect/transcribe vol.58 f.65 sack-8 list and enumerate every named manuscript/category.
Search all Cambridge volumes for explicit sack number 8 and match members to the sack-8 list.
Inspect vol.55 f.129v and test whether its Box 3 contents match any box in RAS BHH/11/1.
Inspect vol.94 ff.40-44 and transcribe bundle numbers/categories, then search for those numbers on surviving covers and notebooks.
Recover explicit shipment numbers on vol.4 and vol.5 notebook covers.
Build a graph whose nodes are historical containers and modern shelfmarks, with edge strength based on surviving identifiers rather than thematic similarity.
